audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused specs: EIP-1052 (EXTCODEHASH opcode), Prague LOG instructions, EIP-7801 (etha P2P subprotocol), Shanghai fork index, EIP-214 (STATICCALL), EIP-2481 (eth/66 request-response), EIP-7610 (CREATE collision reverts), EIP-7702 (EOA code delegation), EIP-4 (EIP process), and EIP-2364 (eth/64 forkid).

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via etha Subprotocol (EIP-7801)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: etha P2P subprotocol messages (BlockHeaders, BlockBodies, Receipts requests/responses)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers communicate via etha subprotocol for block data exchange. Peers can send malformed messages, invalid headers, or flood with requests. All peer data requires full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Shanghai Fork)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC transaction submission and state queries
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions and query state via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All user input is untrusted and must be validated against Shanghai fork rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer (Shanghai Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagate blocks that must be fully validated against Shanghai consensus rules before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via eth/66 Protocol (EIP-2481)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth/66 request-response messages with request IDs
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers send eth/66 messages with request IDs for correlation. Malicious peers can send mismatched IDs, oversized responses, or flood with requests. All messages require validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Attacker via CREATE/CREATE2 Collision (EIP-7610)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction executing CREATE/CREATE2 targeting address with residual storage
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attackers can craft transactions targeting addresses with leftover storage/nonce from previous deployments. EIP-7610 reverts creation at addresses with non-empty storage or nonce, preventing resurrection attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via SET_CODE Transaction (EIP-7702)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Type-4 transaction with authorization_list for EOA delegation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit delegation transactions with authorization tuples. Signatures must be cryptographically verified. Chain ID, nonce, and existing code checks provide defense-in-depth. Replay attacks possible across chains without chain_id binding.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via eth/64 Forkid (EIP-2364)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth/64 Status message with ENRForkID (fork hash + fork next)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers present fork identifiers during handshake. Malicious peers can present incorrect fork IDs to cause connection to incompatible chains. Fork hash must be validated against local chain configuration.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All peer messages validated for structure, size limits, and protocol compliance. Invalid messages trigger peer disconnect. Block headers and bodies verified against consensus rules before state application.
Transactions validated for signature, nonce, gas, and Shanghai-specific rules. Invalid transactions rejected before pool insertion.
Blocks fully validated against Shanghai consensus rules including withdrawals processing. Invalid blocks rejected and peer penalized.
Request IDs must match between request and response. Responses validated for size limits. Unsolicited responses or mismatched IDs trigger peer disconnect.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: CREATE/CREATE2 opcode execution with collision check (EIP-7610)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Target address checked for non-zero nonce or non-empty storage before code deployment. Collision detected = creation reverts with all gas consumed. Prevents storage resurrection attacks.

ECDSA signature validation, chain_id verification, nonce matching, and existing delegation code checks. Invalid authorizations silently skipped per spec. 0xef0100 prefix uniquely identifies delegated code.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: eth/64 Status handshake with ENRForkID validation (EIP-2364)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Fork hash computed as CRC32 of genesis hash + fork block numbers. Incompatible fork IDs result in immediate disconnect. Prevents connections to nodes on different chains or forks.
